evidence: src/domain/errors.ts: DomainError base, with ValidationError, NotFoundError, InsufficientStockError and InvalidTransitionError as subclasses; order.ts and product.ts throw only these
src/domain/order.ts: LIFECYCLE and CANCELLABLE define the state machine in one place; advanceTo delegates to cancel and nextState
src/domain/product.ts: available getter and ensureAvailable are the single source of the stock availability rule, reused by reserve
src/domain/order.ts Order.place and src/domain/product.ts assertPositiveInteger both check Number.isInteger(quantity) && quantity > 0. This is minor cross-aggregate duplication in different contexts

src/domain/repositories.ts: ProductRepository and OrderRepository depend only on the domain types Product, Order and OrderState; IdGenerator and Clock are interfaces the domain depends on, kept in a file named for repositories
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The src/domain module is one cohesive domain model. errors.ts defines the DomainError hierarchy. order.ts holds the Order aggregate and its lifecycle state machine. product.ts holds the Product aggregate with its stock invariants. repositories.ts declares the persistence and environment interfaces. Both aggregates use their abstractions the same way: private constructors, validating static factories (Order.place, Product.create), snapshot() for read models, and only DomainError subclasses for failures. The lifecycle rules (LIFECYCLE, CANCELLABLE) live only in order.ts, and the availability rule (available, ensureAvailable) lives only in product.ts. Two near-duplications exist. First, the positive-integer quantity check appears in Order.place (order.ts) and in assertPositiveInteger (product.ts). These guard different contexts (order line validity and stock reservation), so this is acceptable, though a shared quantity value object would unify it. Second, the 'quantity > reserved' guard repeats in Product.release and Product.dispatch within one class. Also, repositories.ts declares IdGenerator and Clock, which are not repositories. That is a naming nit, not a split into unrelated concerns. Nothing bypasses the module's abstractions.
